prerequisites: Ability to analyze, synthesize, and interpret.
Ability to work in groups, respect deadlines, and communicate well with group members.
Ability to report orally and in writing.

learning_outcomes.text: To clarify and illustrate concepts from theoretical courses.
To sharpen communication skills (oral and written reporting, use of word processor, communication in languages other than the mother tongue, ...).
To acquire 'sense of reality': by critical observation, learn to assess the usability and limitations of theoretical concepts and experimental techniques.
To gain experience with group work and work organization.
To develop analytical thinking and a sense of synthesis.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to quantitative chemical analysis of materials
Application of characterization techniques (mechanical, physical, chemical tests)
Determining if a component is made from the correct material
Use of appropriate and relevant techniques
Presentation of a possible alternative in material choice
How the component was manufactured and treated
Reasons for certain properties to be established
assessment_rules: Assessment is based on continuous evaluation, including participation during contact moments, presentation, and a report. Oral and written reporting are required, sometimes with individual exercises. The technical-scientific quality of the final result is always decisive in determining the final score.
institution: KU Leuven - Faculty of Engineering Science
degree: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen (Bachelor of Engineering Science, Leuven)
